mainTopic: An animal bought from a non-Jew: when is its next baby a sure בכור, and how do רבי ישמעאל, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא disagree about an unseen discharge (טינוף)?
overview: The גמרא first settles, in the words of רבא, that רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority (מיעוטא). רבינא offers another way: even the רבנן, who usually follow the majority, would not rely on a majority that depends on an action, like an animal becoming pregnant. Then a ברייתא lays out רבי ישמעאל's age rules for an animal bought from a non-Jew. Below a set age its next male baby is surely a בכור, and above that age it is a ספק. רבי יהושע says רבי ישמעאל erred, because a small sign like a murky discharge (טינוף) or an afterbirth also exempts an animal. רבי עקיבא rejects age rules altogether and goes only by what is known. The גמרא then explains that רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע argue about worrying over a discharge nobody saw. It gives two ways to fit this with רבי ישמעאל worrying about the minority. Finally, it asks how רבי יהושע's received tradition differs from his own view, and answers either with זעירי's thirty-day rule or with whether an animal can give birth early.

steps.title: It is clear: רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, who takes the minority into account.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is clear that רבי ישמעאל agrees with רבי מאיר, who is concerned about the minority.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא closes the earlier question by deciding that רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר's view of worrying about the minority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an animal is past the young age, most animals that age have already given birth. Still, רבי ישמעאל calls the next baby only a ספק, not clearly exempt. That shows he does not rely fully on the majority and still worries about the few that never gave birth.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear; the גמרא's settled conclusion

phrases.english: It is clear that Rabbi Yishmael
holds like Rabbi Meir,
who is concerned about the minority.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְחַוַּורְתָּא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion, from before this section, about which view רבי ישמעאל follows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי ישמעאל follows רבי מאיר and worries about the minority.

steps.title: רבינא: even the רבנן agree when the majority depends on an action
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says רבי ישמעאל could even follow the רבנן, because the רבנן only follow a majority that does not depend on an action.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: You can even say he follows the רבנן. The רבנן follow the majority only when that majority does not depend on an action. When the majority does depend on an action, they do not follow it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a second way to explain רבי ישמעאל, so he does not have to follow רבי מאיר specifically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain majority, which is just how nature works, is reliable for the רבנן. Whether an animal has given birth depends on something happening first, such as becoming pregnant, so that kind of majority is weaker. Here even the רבנן would not lean on it.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying the רבנן never follow the majority. He is saying they do not follow one specific kind of majority, one that depends on an action.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important split between two kinds of majority, one built into nature and one that depends on something happening.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
You can even say he follows the Rabbis,
when the Rabbis follow the majority,
it is with a majority that does not depend on an action,
but a majority that depends on an action, no.
phrases.notes: Here the action is something like the animal mating and getting pregnant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation, so that רבי ישמעאל can fit the רבנן as well.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל must hold like רבי מאיר, against the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even the רבנן do not follow a majority that depends on an action, so רבי ישמעאל can agree with them.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists the ages for goat, ewe, cow, and donkey
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives רבי ישמעאל's age limits: under a set age the baby is surely a בכור, and above it the case is a ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A goat in its first year, the baby surely goes to the כהן; after that it is a ספק. A ewe in its second year, the baby surely goes to the כהן; after that it is a ספק. A cow in its third year, the baby surely goes to the כהן; after that it is a ספק. A donkey is like a cow. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: a donkey in its fourth year. Up to here are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lays out רבי ישמעאל's full rule for each kind of animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each animal has an age before which it most likely has not given birth yet, so its next male baby is surely a בכור for the כהן. Past that age it may already have given birth, so the status is a ספק. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה gives the donkey one more year.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly goes to the כהן as a בכור

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A goat in its first year, the baby certainly goes to the priest,
from then on, it is uncertain.
A ewe in its second year, the baby certainly goes to the priest,
from then on, it is uncertain.
A cow in its third year, the baby certainly goes to the priest,
from then on, it is uncertain.
A donkey is like a cow.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
A donkey in its fourth year.
Up to here are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that quotes רבי ישמעאל's rule in full.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Below a set age for each animal, the baby is surely a בכור; above that age, it is a ספק.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: you erred, because small signs of a birth also exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects רבי ישמעאל's rule, since an animal is exempted not only by a full baby but also by signs such as a discharge or an afterbirth.
steps.simpleTranslation: When these words were said before רבי יהושע, he told them: Go tell רבי ישמעאל, you made a mistake! If only a real baby exempted the animal, you would be right. But the sign of a baby in a small animal is a murky discharge, in a large animal it is an afterbirth, and in a woman it is a fetal sac or an afterbirth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי ישמעאל's age rules and says they are built on a wrong assumption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's ages assume only a full birth could have exempted the animal. Even a very young animal might have passed a discharge or an afterbirth, and that also counts as a first birth. So we can never be sure a young animal's next baby is a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: Is exempted from the next בכור
A murky discharge from the womb
Small animal (sheep or goat) / large animal (cow)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל relies on age, but רבי יהושע says small signs of an earlier birth also exempt an animal, so age cannot prove it never gave birth.

phrases.english: When these words were said before Rabbi Yehoshua,
he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: צְאוּ אִמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: טָעִיתָ!
phrases.english: Go out and say to Rabbi Yishmael: You erred!
If the animal were exempted only by a baby,
it would be as you say,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא סִימַן הַוָּולָד בִּבְהֵמָה דַּקָּה — טִינּוּף,
phrases.english: but the sign of a baby in a small animal is a murky discharge,
and in a large animal, an afterbirth,
and in a woman, a fetal sac or an afterbirth.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְאוּ אִמְרוּ לוֹ לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: טָעִיתָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with רבי יהושע's challenge to רבי ישמעאל's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's age limits for 'certainly a בכור'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier pregnancy can leave only a small sign, such as a discharge or an afterbirth, and that also exempts the animal. So even a young animal might already be exempt.

steps.title: רבי יהושע gives his own age rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says a goat that had a discharge at six months can give birth within its first year, and a sheep that had a discharge in its first year can give birth within its second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I myself do not say so. Rather, a goat that had a discharge at six months can give birth within its first year, and a ewe that had a discharge in its first year can give birth within its second year.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע continues his words from the ברייתא. After passing on the view of others, he now gives his own rule: an animal can have a discharge (טינוף) and still give birth within the same year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 he reported that a discharge can also exempt an animal from בכורה. Now he adds that a discharge does not stop the animal from giving birth soon afterward. A goat that discharged at six months can still give birth within its first year, so a birth within the year does not prove there was no earlier discharge. The גמרא later asks how this differs from the view he reported (Steps 13–15).

keyTerms.meaning: A murky discharge from the womb, like an early miscarriage

phrases.english: But I myself do not say so;
rather, a goat that expelled a discharge at six months old
can give birth within its first year;
a ewe that expelled a discharge in its first year
can give birth within two years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יהושע's words and gives his own positive rule after his rejection in Step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat can have a discharge at six months and give birth within its first year; a ewe can have a discharge in its first year and give birth within its second year.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא goes only by what we know
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא does not use age rules. If we know the animal gave birth before, the כהן gets nothing. If we know it did not, the baby goes to the כהן. If we are unsure, the owner eats it once it has a blemish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: I did not come to this way of measuring. Rather, whenever it is known that the animal already gave birth, the כהן has nothing here. Whenever it is known that it did not give birth, the baby goes to the כהן. If it is uncertain, the owner may eat it once it has a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion in the ברייתא. רבי עקיבא rejects using age to decide, and rules only by what we actually know.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע both set age limits. רבי עקיבא throws out that whole approach. In a case of doubt, the baby is not given to the כהן. Still, the owner cannot treat it like a normal animal, so he eats it only after it gets a blemish (מום).

keyTerms.meaning: A measure or method of deciding
It has already given birth (had its first baby)
A blemish that makes an animal unfit for the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנִי לֹא בָּאתִי לִידֵי מִדָּה זוֹ,
phrases.english: I have not come to this method;
phrases.notes: He means the system of deciding by the animal's age.

phrases.english: rather, any animal that is known to have already given birth
the priest has nothing here;

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁלֹּא בִּיכְּרָה — הֲרֵי זוֹ לַכֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: and any that has not given birth, this goes to the priest;
if uncertain, it is eaten in its blemish by the owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֲנִי לֹא בָּאתִי לִידֵי מִדָּה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the same ברייתא that rejects the age-based rules of the earlier opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Go only by known facts: if it is known the animal gave birth before, the כהן gets nothing. If it is known it did not, the baby goes to the כהן. If it is a ספק, the owner eats it after it gets a blemish.

steps.title: What do רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע argue about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the argument is about. It suggests they argue over whether a discharge exempts an animal from בכורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע argue about? Shall we say they argue about whether a discharge exempts? רבי ישמעאל holds that a discharge does not exempt, and רבי יהושע holds that a discharge does exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now analyzes the ברייתא. It asks what the real point of argument is and offers a first suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the whole argument is about a discharge itself. According to it, רבי ישמעאל holds that a discharge does not count as a birth, while רבי יהושע holds that it does. The next step will test this suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may reject)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree,
Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yehoshua?
Shall we say they disagree about whether a discharge exempts?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר טִינּוּף אֵינוֹ פּוֹטֵר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds a discharge does not exempt,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds a discharge exempts?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא ends, the גמרא begins to analyze the argument inside it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the basic point of disagreement between רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע?

steps.title: The argument is about worrying over an unseen discharge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees that a discharge we actually see exempts the animal. The argument is only about whether we worry that a discharge happened without anyone seeing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we see that it had a discharge, everyone agrees that a discharge exempts. Here they argue about whether we worry about a discharge. רבי ישמעאל holds we do not worry about a discharge, and רבי יהושע holds we do worry about a discharge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from Step 7. It then explains what the argument really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that a discharge exempts. The question is about a case where nobody saw anything. רבי ישמעאל assumes nothing happened, so the next baby is a בכור. רבי יהושע worries that a hidden discharge may have happened, so the next baby is only a ספק.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי ישמעאל holds a discharge is meaningless. He agrees that a discharge we see exempts. He only refuses to worry about one that nobody saw.

phrases.english: If we see that it expelled a discharge,
everyone agrees
that a discharge exempts;
and here they disagree about whether we worry about a discharge:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר: אֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין לְטִינּוּף,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds: we do not worry about a discharge,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds: we do worry about a discharge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דַּחֲזֵינָא דְּטַינִּוף דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested explanation in Step 7 and replaces it with the real point of argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע argue over whether a discharge exempts at all.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A discharge that we see exempts according to everyone. The real argument is only about worrying over a discharge nobody saw.

steps.title: But רבא said רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: how can רבי ישמעאל not worry about a hidden discharge, when רבא said he follows רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority?
steps.simpleTranslation: And he does not worry? But רבא said: It is clear that רבי ישמעאל holds like רבי מאיר, who worries about the minority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from Step 8, using רבא's conclusion from Step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that רבי ישמעאל takes even unlikely possibilities into account. A hidden discharge is just such an unlikely possibility. So it seems רבי ישמעאל should worry about it, and that contradicts Step 8.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a contradiction)
Takes the minority (an unlikely possibility) into account

phrases.english: And he does not worry?
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי ישמעאל, who was just said not to worry about an unseen discharge.

phrases.english: But didn't Rava say:

phrases.aramaic: מְחַוַּורְתָּא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: It is clear that Rabbi Yishmael holds like Rabbi Meir,
who worries about the minority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 8's claim that רבי ישמעאל does not worry about a hidden discharge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 8 that רבי ישמעאל holds אין חוששין לטינוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא established that רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority. A hidden discharge is a minority possibility, so he should worry about it.

steps.title: He worries only when it leads to a stricter result
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority only when that worry makes the law stricter, not when it makes it more lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he worries, it is to be strict. To be lenient, he does not worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. רבי ישמעאל's worry about the minority applies only in one direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Worrying about a hidden discharge would turn the next baby from a sure בכור into a ספק, which is easier on the owner. That is a leniency, so רבי ישמעאל does not take that small chance into account. This way Step 1 and Step 8 both stand.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהושע both agree that a seen discharge exempts. They argue over an unseen one. רבי ישמעאל does not worry about it, because he worries about the minority only to be strict.

phrases.english: When he worries, it is to be strict;
to be lenient, he does not worry.
phrases.notes: Here, worrying would make the baby only a ספק, so the owner keeps it. That is the lenient side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 9 by limiting when רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the principle: worrying about the minority applies only when it leads to a stricter ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority, he should also worry about a hidden discharge.
steps.terutzMaskana: He worries about the minority only when it leads to a stricter ruling. Worrying about a hidden discharge would be lenient, so he ignores it.

steps.title: Second answer: the argument is whether an animal can give birth within its year after a discharge
steps.stepSummary: Here רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority whether that makes the law stricter or more lenient. The argument is really about whether an animal that had a discharge can still give birth within its first year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: רבי ישמעאל worries about the minority whether it leads to a leniency or a stringency. Here they argue about whether an animal that had a discharge can recover and give birth within its first year. רבי ישמעאל holds that it cannot. So since this animal gave birth, it surely never had a discharge. רבי יהושע holds that it can recover and give birth within its first year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the challenge from Step 9. This time רבי ישמעאל does worry about the minority in every case, so the גמרא must move the argument to a different question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this answer, רבי ישמעאל has no reason to worry, because a discharge and a birth within the first year cannot both happen. So the birth itself proves there was no discharge, and the baby is a sure בכור. רבי יהושע thinks both can happen, so the doubt remains.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you wish, say": opens a second, different answer
Whether it makes the law more lenient or stricter
An animal that gives off a murky discharge from the womb
Within its first year of life

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not build on Step 10. It replaces it. In Step 10 רבי ישמעאל worries only when that makes the law stricter. Here he always worries, but in this case nothing is left to worry about.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
whether it leads to leniency or to stringency, he is concerned,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי ישמעאל, who worries about the minority.

phrases.english: and here, about an animal that discharges and then recovers
and gives birth within its year, they disagree.
For רבי ישמעאל holds:
an animal that discharges does not recover
and give birth within its year,
and since this one gave birth,
it certainly did not discharge.
And רבי יהושע holds:
an animal that discharges does recover
and gives birth within its year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: בֵּין לְקוּלָּא בֵּין לְחוּמְרָא חָיֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the challenge of Step 9, in place of the answer in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a factual question about animals, so רבי ישמעאל's worry about the minority does not apply here.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל ignores a hidden discharge even though he usually worries about the minority.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל does worry, but a birth within the first year proves no discharge happened. רבי יהושע disagrees with that fact.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's own view on when an animal can give birth after a discharge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהושע from the ברייתא. A goat that had a discharge at six months gives birth within its first year. A ewe that had a discharge in its first year gives birth within its second year.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I do not say so. Rather, a goat that had a discharge at six months old gives birth within its first year. A ewe that had a discharge during its first year gives birth within its second year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא, where רבי יהושע gives his own opinion. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, רבי יהושע had passed on what he received from others. Now he says "but I do not say so" and gives his own view. Both views agree that an animal can give birth within a year of a discharge, so it is not yet clear how they differ.

keyTerms.meaning: "But I do not say so": the speaker gives his own view

phrases.english: But I do not say so;
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהושע speaking, moving away from the tradition he just passed on.

phrases.english: rather, a goat that discharged at six months old
gives birth within its year,
a ewe that discharged in its first year
gives birth within two years.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the argument about רבי ישמעאל and returns to the ברייתא to look at רבי יהושע's personal opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat that discharged at six months can give birth within its first year. A ewe that discharged in its first year can give birth within its second year.

steps.title: How does רבי יהושע's tradition differ from his own view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the tradition רבי יהושע received and his own opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference is there between his tradition and his own reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: Both opinions seem to say the same thing, so the גמרא asks where they actually lead to different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that an animal can give birth within a year after a discharge. So the גמרא wants a specific case where the two would rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: His tradition: what he received from his teachers
His own reasoning: his personal view

phrases.english: What difference is there between
his tradition and his own reasoning?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the opinion just quoted in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where רבי יהושע's tradition and his own view lead to different rulings.

steps.title: The difference: a goat that discharged at the end of six months, and זעירי's thirty-day rule
steps.stepSummary: The difference is a goat that had a discharge at the end of its sixth month. The tradition accepts זעירי's rule that a discharge blocks pregnancy for thirty days. רבי יהושע's own view does not accept it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a goat that had a discharge at the end of its sixth month. They differ over זעירי's rule, because זעירי said that a real discharge is followed by at least thirty days without pregnancy. His tradition accepts זעירי's rule. His own reasoning does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by giving a case where the two views rule differently. The difference turns on זעירי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A goat is pregnant for five months. If it had a discharge at the end of month six and still gave birth by the end of the year, it must have become pregnant within about a month of the discharge. The tradition follows זעירי: pregnancy that soon means the discharge did not count, so the baby is a בכור. רבי יהושע's own view rejects זעירי, so the discharge still counts and the baby is not a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: A murky discharge from the womb
He accepts / he does not accept (a certain rule)
There is a difference between them

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for רבי ישמעאל. In Step 10, he worries about the minority only when that makes the law stricter. In Step 11, he always worries, but he holds that a discharge and a birth within the first year cannot both happen. רבי יהושע's tradition and his own view differ only over זעירי's thirty-day rule, in the case of a goat that had a discharge at the end of six months.
steps.confusionAlert: The text does not spell out the math. The goat's five-month pregnancy is what forces it to have become pregnant within thirty days of the discharge. That is why זעירי's rule makes a difference here.

phrases.english: Where it discharged at the end of six months,
phrases.notes: He means a goat. To give birth by the end of the year, it must have become pregnant soon after the discharge.

phrases.english: and the difference between them is the rule of זעירי,
for זעירי said:
there is no discharge with less than thirty days.
phrases.notes: A real discharge is followed by at least thirty days without pregnancy. A pregnancy sooner than that means it was not a real discharge.

phrases.english: According to his tradition, it accepts זעירי's rule;
according to his own reasoning, he does not accept זעירי's rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁטִּינְּפָה בְּסוֹף שִׁשָּׁה, וְאִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ דִּזְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Take a goat that discharged at the end of six months and gave birth within its year. The tradition accepts זעירי, so the discharge does not count and the baby is a בכור. רבי יהושע's own view rejects זעירי, so the discharge counts and the animal is exempt from בכורה.

steps.title: Another answer: both accept זעירי, but they argue about early births
steps.stepSummary: Both sides accept זעירי's thirty-day rule. They disagree about whether an animal can give birth after a pregnancy that has not completed its full months.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: everyone agrees with זעירי. Here they argue about whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months, meaning early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question from step 13 about what difference there is between רבי יהושע's tradition and his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the difference was whether זעירי's thirty-day rule is accepted. Now both sides accept it. The case is still a goat with a discharge at the end of its sixth month. After the thirty days she has only just enough time left in the year, so the question becomes whether a birth can come before the pregnancy finishes its full months. One side says it can, so the birth still falls within the first year. The other side says it cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
Everyone: both sides agree on this point
Incomplete or cut-short months, a pregnancy that does not reach its full length

steps.confusionAlert: This does not take back the case from step 14. It is still the goat with a discharge at the end of its sixth month. Only the reason for the disagreement changes.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
that everyone accepts the rule of זעירי,
phrases.notes: This is זעירי's rule from step 14, that a discharge blocks pregnancy for thirty days.

phrases.english: and here, they disagree about whether an animal gives birth after incomplete months;
phrases.notes: "Here" means the goat with a discharge at the end of its sixth month. Incomplete months means giving birth early, before the full term.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 13's question and replaces step 14's explanation that the sides differ over זעירי's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between the tradition רבי יהושע received and his own opinion (asked in step 13).
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both accept זעירי. The difference is whether an animal can give birth after incomplete months, in the case of a goat with a discharge at the end of its sixth month.
